extracted.intended_audience: Chief, Plans Staff (DDS) and Office of Medical Services management / OMS division and staff chiefs
extracted.subtask_description: Internal memorandum reporting projected Office of Medical Services goals and planned implementation actions for OMB Circular A-44 over the period 1 January–30 June 1971, emphasizing management effectiveness, program planning participation, and cost reduction through laboratory automation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting period for projected goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Report of projected goals of the Office of Medical Services for the period 1 January-30 June 1971 is submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The memorandum explicitly frames the goals and expected accomplishments for the six-month window 1 Jan–30 Jun 1971; progress and expectations should be assessed against this reporting period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management Effectiveness Goals — Improved operating efficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: During this six months period we expect an improvement in operating efficiency through the continued development of a practice already started. This is the practice of bringing OMS division and staff chiefs more effectively into the program planning process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operationalizing this goal requires (a) involving OMS division and staff chiefs — who are MDs or PhDs oriented to professional aspects — more directly in PPB-type program planning; (b) drafting the OMS Program Plan for FY 1973–1977 in Jan–Feb 1971 with close collaboration between division/staff chiefs and planning officials; and (c) producing a program submission to which these officials have made significant contributions. The memorandum places emphasis on experiential learning: participation should give division/staff chiefs planning experience that improves future planning and operating efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of PPB (Program Planning and Budget) type planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Program planning -- particularly the PPB type -- is a different experience requiring special attention by the components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize PPB as a distinct planning approach requiring special attention and support for non-planning professionals; ensure planning officials guide division/staff chiefs through PPB processes so they can contribute meaningfully to program submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost Reduction Goals — Reduction in unit cost for laboratory testing materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduction in unit cost for laboratory testing materials: The period 1 January-30 June 1971 will be the first full six months period for the automated multiphasic biochemical profiling in the Clinical Division laboratory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt automated multiphasic biochemical profiling (SMA 12 Jr.) to lower reagent costs: the SMA 12 Jr. runs 12 tests per sample (30 samples/hour). Reagents for the SMA 12 Jr. cost $2 per battery of 12 tests vs. $1 per manual test (i.e., $12 for 12 manual tests), yielding reagent costs roughly one sixth of prior manual procedures. Evaluate cost savings by comparing reagent/unit costs and throughput gains; treat reagent cost per battery and processing capacity as key metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expand access via multiphasic screening enabled by automation
rubrics_metrics.description: This economy makes multiphasic screening appropriate. Our program plans provide for such a screening program to enable us to be accessible to many of the Agency employees that we do not now see.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage reduced per-test costs and increased throughput to implement a multiphasic screening program aimed at increasing accessibility to Agency employees currently not served. Measure success by uptake among previously unserved employees and by continuity of reduced unit costs sustaining expanded screening.
